title: Give the factory a CLI-based delivery loop for parked questions
description:
REPLACES the cancelled endpoint tick. The factory reaches into ticks through the tk CLI; ticks never reaches out. Zero Go coupling in either direction.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so build on it rather than beside it:
  tk list --awaiting     finds parked questions
  .tick/pending          holds the entries
  tk answer <id> <answer> resolves one, and 'the question answered is the oldest one still open on the tick'
  tk ask --collect        prints every settled question as a JSON line and drains it

Read tk ask/answer --help before designing — the surface is richer than it looks and an orchestrator/pane relay is answered by the question id rather than the tick id, which matters for routing.

THE LOOP: discover parked questions, deliver each to Telegram with its project/epic/tick context, and write the human's reply back with tk answer. The Worker already owns the bot and its webhook, so inbound answers arrive there; this closes the other half.

DESIGN QUESTIONS THAT ARE THE ACTUAL WORK:
- WHERE DOES IT RUN? The Worker cannot exec tk. So this is either the factory's Go side on a machine that has both, or a sandbox-side loop. Decide and say why. This is the question that determines whether the feature is 'reachable when your laptop is closed' — which is the entire point of the factory — so a design that only works while a laptop is awake has missed it.
- CONTEXT. contracts/message-context.json pins the project/epic/tick shape across languages. Reuse it; do not invent a second message shape.
- IDEMPOTENCY. A question must not be delivered twice, and a retried answer must not double-resolve. tk answer resolves the OLDEST open question on a tick — understand what that means for concurrent delivery before relying on it.
- FAILURE. tk unreachable, factory unreachable, Telegram unconfigured are three different facts. Keep them apart.

SCOPE: the factory side only. Do NOT touch cmd/tk/cmd/** or internal/operator/** — sibling ticks own those.
acceptance_criteria: The factory discovers parked questions via the tk CLI, delivers them with contract-conforming context, and resolves them via tk answer. Where it runs is decided in writing, with the laptop-closed requirement addressed. Duplicate delivery and double-resolution are both prevented and tested. The three failure states are distinguishable. Factory suite green; no new Go import from ticks.
